description: Statically derived by reading app/cbl/COCRDUPC.cbl, never captured from a run: the COBOL cannot be executed in this environment - there is no z/OS and no CICS emulator, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository - so every value below is read out of the source, the copybooks, the symbolic map and the fixture rather than recorded from an execution (practice B12, risk R-A). This is the folder's YEAR-OUT-OF-RANGE rejection - paragraph 1260-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR at :913-947 - and it carries TWO findings. The first is the rejection itself, and specifically the storage the range test reads: the year is held in one four-byte span addressed BOTH as alphanumeric text AND as a number, with the 88 that decides the case declared on the numeric view. The second is structural and is the reason this case exists at this position in the folder: 1260 IS THE ONE PARAGRAPH IN THE SIX-EDIT CHAIN WHOSE FLAG ORDERING DIFFERS FROM ITS FIVE SIBLINGS, and that divergence is documented here rather than normalised away (practices B4 and B5). The construction comes first, because reaching 1260 with a clean message slot takes more than an invalid year. Row 1 of fixtures/carddata.txt is seeded and snapshotted, so CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME is the upper-cased 'ANIYA VON' that case06.json derived through the INSPECT CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME CONVERTING LIT-LOWER TO LIT-UPPER at :1356-1358, and CCUP-OLD-EXPYEAR/EXPMON/EXPDAY are '2023'/'03'/'09' - the three reference-modified slices (1:4)/(6:2)/(9:2) that :1361-1366 takes out of the ten-byte 'YYYY-MM-DD' of CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE, the copybook's own misspelling at app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy:9, preserved verbatim because renaming it would break field-for-field diffing (requirement I1). CCUP-OLD-CRDSTCD is 'Y'. The resubmitted EXPYEARI is '2149', which is a DELIBERATELY OUT-OF-RANGE INPUT AND NOT FIXTURE DATA: an exhaustive scan of all fifty rows shows the stored year span holds only 2023, 2024 and 2025, every one of them inside 1950 THRU 2099, so no seeded record could supply a year above the ceiling and no arrangement of rows would produce one - the operator's keyboard is the only source, which is exactly the path this case tests (practice B1). CRDNAMEI, CRDSTCDI and EXPMONI are resubmitted UNCHANGED from the snapshot so that 1230, 1240 and 1250 all take their success limbs and write no message, which is what makes 1260's message the first one admitted through the IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF guard and leaves the single highlight and the single cursor position below unambiguous. EIBCALEN is 489, which is 160 + 329 - the width COMMON-RETURN hands back at :549-557, where 160 is CARDDEMO-COMMAREA summed mechanically from app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy as 4 + 8 + 4 + 8 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 9 + 25 + 25 + 25 + 11 + 1 + 16 + 7 + 7 and 329 is WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA at :274-321 as 1 (CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION) + 89 (CCUP-OLD-DETAILS: 11 + 16 + 3 + 59) + 89 (CCUP-NEW-DETAILS) + 150 (CARD-UPDATE-RECORD: 16 + 11 + 3 + 50 + 10 + 1 + 59) (practice B11). So the :388 guard fails EQUAL TO 0, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is LIT-CCLISTPGM ('COCRDLIC', :227-228) rather than LIT-MENUPGM, and the ELSE at :396-400 restores CARDDEMO-COMMAREA from DFHCOMMAREA(1:160) and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA from DFHCOMMAREA(161:329), so the inbound ids and the whole CCUP-OLD-* snapshot SURVIVE. The case contract keys a commarea value by the copybook name and admits the CDEMO- items of the shared area plus the WS- items of the receiving program's own extension; COCRDUPC names its extension items CCUP-*, which neither form covers, so the extension is declared under the one legal name the source itself gives the whole span, WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, carrying the exact 329-byte image that single MOVE restores. Its bytes decode as CCUP-CHANGE-ACTION [1] 'S' (88 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :281), then CCUP-OLD-DETAILS [2-90] as CCUP-OLD-ACCTID [2-12] '00000000050', CCUP-OLD-CARDID [13-28] '0500024453765740', CCUP-OLD-CVV-CD [29-31] '747', CCUP-OLD-CRDNAME [32-81] 'ANIYA VON' padded to 50, CCUP-OLD-EXPYEAR [82-85] '2023', CCUP-OLD-EXPMON [86-87] '03', CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY [88-89] '09' and CCUP-OLD-CRDSTCD [90] 'Y' - the snapshot exactly as case06.json derived it - then CCUP-NEW-DETAILS [91-179] and CARD-UPDATE-RECORD [180-329] as spaces, which is the state the previous turn left and is inert on this path in both halves: :586 INITIALIZEs CCUP-NEW-DETAILS before a single byte of it is read, and CARD-UPDATE-RECORD is built only at :1461-1475, inside a 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING this case never enters. The same nuance case11.json and case12.json record is recorded here for the same reason: CCUP-NEW-DETAILS is PIC X throughout so an INITIALIZE genuinely leaves it spaces, whereas CARD-UPDATE-ACCT-ID at :316 is PIC 9(11) and CARD-UPDATE-CVV-CD at :317 is PIC 9(03), and INITIALIZE sets a numeric item to ZEROS - so a strict reading of the :506 and :519 INITIALIZE of the whole 329-byte group would leave zeros in those two sub-spans rather than spaces. The span is nevertheless declared exactly as its two sibling fixtures declare it, because all three depart from the same case06.json-produced state and none of the three paths reads those bytes: the difference is unobservable, and stating it is better than leaving a reader to work out which of three sibling fixtures is wrong (practice B4). CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1 (REENTER) and ENTER is admitted unchanged by :413-424, because :414 lists CCARD-AID-ENTER among the four combinations it accepts. The ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :429 is then gate G30 read downwards: arm one (:435-439) needs PF03 or a done/failed state with CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET equal to LIT-CCLISTMAPSET, and the AID is ENTER with the state 'S'; arm two (:482-485) needs CDEMO-PGM-ENTER, which REENTER denies, or CCARD-AID-PFK12, which ENTER denies; arm three (:502-505) needs CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED with CDEMO-PGM-ENTER, or an arrival from LIT-MENUPGM; arm four (:517-518) needs 'C', 'L' or 'F'. So WHEN OTHER at :535 performs 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS, 2000-DECIDE-ACTION and 3000-SEND-MAP as range performs and leaves through GO TO COMMON-RETURN at :542. Reaching 1000-PROCESS-INPUTS is also why this case names a next program: :570-572 move LIT-THISPGM, LIT-THISMAPSET and LIT-THISMAP into CCARD-NEXT-PROG, CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET and CCARD-NEXT-MAP, so the response carries 'COCRDUPC' together with the mapset and the map, the X(8) 'COCRDUP ' of :223-224 landing in a CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET that CVCRD01Y declares X(7). 1100-RECEIVE-MAP :578-636 INITIALIZEs CCUP-NEW-DETAILS at :586 and then normalises each field, mapping '*' or SPACES to LOW-VALUES; EXPYEARI is neither, so :630-635 takes the ELSE limb at :633-634 and moves '2149' VERBATIM into CCUP-NEW-EXPYEAR - no trim, no numeric coercion and no range check happens here, which is why the range test downstream is the only thing standing between the operator and the record. Two source oddities are preserved rather than tidied (practice B5). MOVE EXPDAYI OF CCRDUPAI TO CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY at :621 is UNCONDITIONAL - alone among the six data moves it carries no '*'/SPACES guard - and it is left that way. And CCUP-NEW-CVV-CD is never assigned anywhere in the program, because the COCRDUP map has no CVV field, so it keeps the SPACES the :586 INITIALIZE gave it; this case declines to hide that rather than pinning it, since nothing is written here for it to corrupt. 1200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS :641-715 SETs INPUT-OK at :643 and then finds IF CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED false, so it takes the ELSE CONTINUE at :663-664: 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT and 1220-EDIT-CARD are NOT performed, and neither is the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA at :653 that would have wiped the fifty-nine bytes just received. Execution continues past :667 with SET FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT (:668), SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID and SET FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID (:669-670), and then :671-677 copy the snapshot outwards into CDEMO-ACCT-ID, CDEMO-CARD-NUM, CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME, CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS and the three REDEFINES sub-fields CARD-EXPIRY-DAY, CARD-EXPIRY-MONTH and CARD-EXPIRY-YEAR declared at :115-123 over CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE-X PIC X(10) (4 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10) - the first of this case's two REDEFINES pairs and part of gate G34. THE DETECTOR AT :680-683 HAD TO BE DEFEATED FOR 1260 TO RUN AT ALL, AND IT IS WORTH THE ARITHMETIC. IF (FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(CCUP-NEW-CARDDATA) EQUAL FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(CCUP-OLD-CARDDATA)) compares the whole GROUP and not field by field; from :295-301 and :307-313 each group is CRDNAME X(50) + EXPIRAION-DATE (EXPYEAR X(4) + EXPMON X(2) + EXPDAY X(2)) + CRDSTCD X(1), summing mechanically to 50 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 59 bytes (practice B11), so within the group CRDNAME occupies [1-50], EXPYEAR [51-54], EXPMON [55-56], EXPDAY [57-58] and CRDSTCD [59]. BOTH OPERANDS ARE FOLDED TO UPPER CASE, so a resubmission differing only in letter case would compare EQUAL, NO-CHANGES-DETECTED would be set at :682, the three-way IF at :685-687 would force all four edit flags ISVALID and the GO TO at :692 would skip every edit - that is case09.json's path, and 1260 would never have executed. Worked byte by byte here, UPPER-CASE(OLD) is 'ANIYA VON' padded to 50, then '2023', '03', '09', 'Y' and UPPER-CASE(NEW) is the same 50 bytes, then '2149', '03', '09', 'Y', so the two differ at THREE positions - group bytes 52, 53 and 54, the hundreds, tens and units digits of the year, with group byte 51 identical because both years begin '2'. Every one of those differences is in DIGITS, which no case fold can erase. (case11.json and case12.json defeat the same detector inside the month at group bytes 55 and 56; this case defeats it inside the year, which is the adjacent span, so the three together exercise the detector across both fields of CCUP-NEW-EXPIRAION-DATE.) The comparison fails, NO-CHANGES-DETECTED is NOT set, and the observable consequence is asserted as an absence: the 88 at :187-188, 'No change detected with respect to values fetched.', appears NOWHERE in this expectation. The first limb of :685-687 being false, and the state being 'S' rather than 'N' or 'C', the skip does not fire and execution reaches SET CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK TO TRUE at :696, so THE STATE BECOMES 'E' BEFORE A SINGLE EDIT EXECUTES. That ordering is not incidental - it is what arms the CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK guard on every data-field highlight below, and a translation that set the state after the edits, or only on failure, would paint an unhighlighted screen and still pass most of this folder. The four edits then run in source order at :698-708, and only the last of them fails. 1230-EDIT-NAME :806-840 SUCCEEDS: the blank test at :811-813 fails because the name is populated, :823 moves it into CARD-NAME-CHECK PIC X(50), :824-826 INSPECTs it CONVERTING LIT-ALL-ALPHA-FROM TO LIT-ALL-SPACES-TO, and because 'ANIYA VON' padded to 50 holds nothing but letters and spaces the result is fifty spaces, so IF FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION TRIM(CARD-NAME-CHECK)) = 0 at :828 takes the CONTINUE at :829 and :839 SETs FLG-CARDNAME-ISVALID - the first of the three '1' flags asserted here. 1240-EDIT-CARDSTATUS :845-874 SUCCEEDS too: the blank test at :850-852 fails, :861 moves 'Y' into FLG-YES-NO-CHECK declared at :89-91 as PIC X(1) VALUE 'N' with 88 FLG-YES-NO-VALID VALUES 'Y', 'N', the byte matches the first literal as written, IF FLG-YES-NO-VALID at :863 is TRUE and :864 SETs FLG-CARDSTATUS-ISVALID. 1250-EDIT-EXPIRY-MON :877-908 SUCCEEDS as well: :880 SETs FLG-CARDEXPMON-NOT-OK, the blank test at :883-885 fails, :896 moves '03' into CARD-MONTH-CHECK PIC X(2) whose CARD-MONTH-CHECK-N REDEFINES view at :92-95 evaluates as 3, inside 88 VALID-MONTH VALUES 1 THRU 12, so IF VALID-MONTH at :898 is TRUE and :899 SETs FLG-CARDEXPMON-ISVALID. All three flags are asserted at '1' precisely because they are what make this case's single message, single highlight and single cursor unambiguous - the out-of-range month belongs to case12.json, the lower-case status to case11.json and the non-alphabetic name to case10.json. THE FIRST HEADLINE IS 1260-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR :913-947. Its blank test comes FIRST, at :916-918 - IF CCUP-NEW-EXPYEAR EQUAL LOW-VALUES OR EQUAL SPACES OR EQUAL ZEROS - and it FAILS, because '2149' is populated; that branch, and the FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-BLANK it sets at :920, belong to case14.json and not here. SET FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-NOT-OK TO TRUE then runs at :930, leaving the flag at '0'. :932 MOVEs CCUP-NEW-EXPYEAR TO CARD-YEAR-CHECK, AND THIS IS GATE G34. :96-99 declares CARD-YEAR-CHECK PIC X(4), then CARD-YEAR-CHECK-N REDEFINES CARD-YEAR-CHECK PIC 9(4), and the condition name 88 VALID-YEAR VALUES 1950 THRU 2099 is declared UNDER CARD-YEAR-CHECK-N - that is, on the NUMERIC view. ONE BACKING SPAN, TWO TYPED ACCESSORS: the MOVE at :932 writes the span as four alphanumeric characters, and the IF at :934 reads the same four bytes as a number. Both directions of the round trip are asserted, because both are load-bearing. Read as text the span holds '2149' exactly, which is what :1117 echoes into EXPYEARO and what :680-683 compared as group bytes 51-54; read as a number the same span evaluates as 2149, which is above the 2099 ceiling and therefore outside 1950 THRU 2099, so IF VALID-YEAR at :934 is FALSE. A translation that kept only the number would still render '2149' correctly by accident, but could not preserve a leading zero in any four-byte year span it was handed, and a translation that kept only the string could not evaluate 1950 THRU 2099 at all without re-deriving the numeric view it had discarded. Neither is a faithful REDEFINES. The ELSE at :936-943 therefore runs: SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE at :937, SET FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-NOT-OK TO TRUE at :938 which merely holds the flag at the '0' :930 already wrote, then, GUARDED BY IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at :939, SET CARD-EXPIRY-YEAR-NOT-VALID TO TRUE - the 88 at :199-200, 'Invalid card expiry year', at twenty-four characters the SHORTEST of the six edit messages - and GO TO 1260-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR-EXIT at :942. The guard ADMITS the message because :384 SET WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF cleared WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) on entry and nothing between there and here has written it: this is the FIRST error on the path, which is exactly why the three sibling edits were deliberately given valid inputs. THE TWO BRANCHES OF THIS PARAGRAPH SHARE ONE MESSAGE, which is why the flag is asserted and not just the text. :922 (blank) and :940 (out of range) both SET CARD-EXPIRY-YEAR-NOT-VALID, so ERRMSGO alone cannot tell the two apart - the same property 1240 and 1250 have; only WS-EDIT-CARDEXPYEAR-FLAG can, and its 88s at :77-80 give FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-NOT-OK '0' here against FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-BLANK ' ' in the blank branch. The '0' is what separates this case from case14.json, and it is observable at one remove through the highlight and the cursor derived below, both of which key off FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-NOT-OK specifically - and the '*' that only the BLANK branch writes is the sharpest tell of all, because it would overwrite the very value the operator has to correct. THE SECOND HEADLINE IS THE ORDERING ASYMMETRY, AND IT IS THIS CASE'S REASON FOR EXISTING BEYOND THE REJECTION. All six edit paragraphs were re-read to establish it rather than assumed. Five of them SET their NOT-OK flag as the paragraph's FIRST executable statement, BEFORE the blank test: 1210-EDIT-ACCOUNT SETs FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :722 before its blank test at :725-727; 1220-EDIT-CARD SETs FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK at :765 before :768-770; 1230-EDIT-NAME SETs FLG-CARDNAME-NOT-OK at :808 before :811-813; 1240-EDIT-CARDSTATUS SETs FLG-CARDSTATUS-NOT-OK at :847 before :850-852; and 1250-EDIT-EXPIRY-MON SETs FLG-CARDEXPMON-NOT-OK at :880 before :883-885. 1260-EDIT-EXPIRY-YEAR DOES NOT: its blank test is the paragraph's first statement at :916-918, and SET FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-NOT-OK does not run until :930 - AFTER the whole blank branch, including that branch's GO TO at :924. THE OBSERVABLE CONSEQUENCE is that when 1260 takes its blank branch it SETs FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-BLANK at :920 and leaves at :924 WITHOUT EVER PASSING THROUGH :930, whereas in each of the five siblings the blank branch has already been preceded by a NOT-OK set that the blank set then overwrites. The end state of the flag happens to coincide - ' ' either way - but the instruction sequence does not, and a translator who 'regularised' the six paragraphs into one shared shape, or who hoisted a common NOT-OK initialisation out of them, would be changing the source rather than translating it. This case does not itself take the blank branch - case14.json does - but it is the case that DOCUMENTS THE ASYMMETRY, because it is the case that executes :930 and can name it. Practice B5: every paragraph is preserved as found, nothing simplified. Practice B4: the divergence is documented rather than silently normalised. One further artefact of the same copy-paste lineage is preserved with it: 1260's own comments at :927-928 still read '* Must be numeric' and '* Must be 1 to 12', carried over from 1250 even though the range this paragraph actually enforces is 1950 THRU 2099. The comment is wrong and it stays wrong - correcting it would be an edit to a reference input, which practice B3 forbids outright. At :710-714 IF INPUT-ERROR CONTINUE ELSE SET CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED, and INPUT-ERROR was set inside 1260, so 'N' is not set and the state remains 'E'. 2000-DECIDE-ACTION :948-1031 is read in source order too: arm (a) WHEN CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED at :954 fails, arm (b) WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK12 at :958 fails because ENTER was pressed, arm (c) WHEN CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS at :971 fails because the state is no longer 'S', and arm (d) WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK at :982-983 matches and CONTINUEs (gate G30, the arm chosen by source order). That single CONTINUE is what prevents any write attempt, because 9200-WRITE-PROCESSING at :1420 is reachable only from the :988-989 arm requiring CCUP-CHANGES-OK-NOT-CONFIRMED together with PF05: no repository call of any kind occurs on this path, not a read, not a read-for-update and not a rewrite, and 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC at :1498 is never entered either. 3000-SEND-MAP :1035-1046 then runs 3100, 3200, 3250, 3300 and 3400 in that order, and that order is load-bearing for the cursor derivation below. 3100 fills CCRDUPAO with LOW-VALUES at :1053 - which is why every colour item starts at x'00', the byte DFHBMSCA names DFHDFCOL - and moves the two active COTTL01Y titles (line 21 of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy is commented out in column 7, so TITLE02O is the active line 22) together with LIT-THISTRANID, LIT-THISPGM and the MM/DD/YY and HH:MM:SS renderings of the pinned clock. 3200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS :1082-1134 runs its ELSE limb because the context is REENTER; CC-ACCT-ID-N and CC-CARD-NUM-N are both non-zero from the :589-605 loads - the ELSE limbs at :594-595 and :603-604, taken because neither key arrived as '*' or SPACES - so ACCTSIDO carries '00000000050' at X(11) and CARDSIDO '0500024453765740' at X(16); and the inner four-arm ordered EVALUATE at :1099 passes over arm one (:1100 CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED, false) and arm two (:1107 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS, false now that the state is 'E') to match arm three at :1113, WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-MADE - the grouping 88 at :282-284 whose values are 'E', 'N', 'C', 'L' and 'F'. Its body at :1114-1123 paints the CCUP-NEW-* values, so THE OFFENDING INPUT IS ECHOED BACK: EXPYEARO is the '2149' the user typed and not the stored '2023'. Honesty about which fields prove that arm choice matters more than the appearance of proof: the name, the status and the month were resubmitted at their snapshot values by construction, so they read identically under arm two, arm three and the WHEN OTHER at :1124-1129, and THE YEAR IS THE ONE FIELD THAT DISTINGUISHES THE ARM BY VALUE HERE - '2149' where the OLD snapshot holds '2023'. That is the exact contrast with case09.json, where the skip left the state at 'S', arm two matched, and the user's typing was DISCARDED in favour of the stored value: one EVALUATE, two arms, opposite treatments of the same screen fields. The day is the exception and is preserved as written: :1122 is a COMMENTED-OUT MOVE CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY and :1123 moves CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY instead, under a source comment explaining that the field is not one the user is allowed to change, so EXPDAYO is taken from the OLD snapshot - and because EXPDAYI is resubmitted as the '09' that 3200 painted and :1285 renders dark, CCUP-NEW-EXPDAY and CCUP-OLD-EXPDAY coincide here, so the choice at :1123 is preserved structurally but is NOT distinguishable by value on this path. Stated rather than overclaimed, exactly as the unconditional :621 is (practices B4 and B5). 3250-SETUP-INFOMSG :1138-1164 is ordered the same way: arm one :1141 CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is false, arm two :1143 CCUP-DETAILS-NOT-FETCHED is false, arm three :1145 CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS is false, and arm four :1147-1148 WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK matches, so SET PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES puts the 88 literal of :164-165 into WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) and :1161 paints INFOMSGO as 'Update card details presented above.' - the trailing full stop is INSIDE the literal, giving thirty-six characters - with four trailing spaces to reach X(40). :1163 then moves WS-RETURN-MSG into the X(80) ERRMSGO, so the twenty-four characters of 'Invalid card expiry year' are followed by fifty-six spaces. Neither CSMSG01Y literal appears: the thank-you and invalid-key texts have zero references anywhere in this program. GATE G38, THE CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK-GUARDED HALF, IS THE REASON THIS CASE CARRIES A COLOUR MAP AT ALL. COCRDUPC does not COPY CSSETATY - its COPY list at :268-359 plus the 'CSSTRPFY' at :1528 contains no such member - so it re-implements the error highlight inline at :1243-1307, AND THE GUARD IS NOT THE SAME FOR EVERY FIELD GROUP. The two search keys are guarded by AND CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :1247 and :1257, and their flags were set ISVALID at :669-670, so neither the '*' nor the DFHRED fires for them here - that half of the gate is proved by case03.json, where 1210 and 1220 do run and both keys redden. The four data fields are guarded by AND CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK instead, and this case is where that guard is satisfied for the expiry year: IF FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-NOT-OK AND CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK at :1298-1301 has a '0' flag from :930 and :938 and an 'E' state from :696, so MOVE DFHRED TO EXPYEARC FIRES and EXPYEARC is the one colour item that differs from DFHDFCOL by an error. Its '*' companion at :1303-1307 requires FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-BLANK and does NOT fire, which is why EXPYEARO keeps the echoed '2149' rather than being overwritten with an asterisk - the two guards are five lines apart, they share a message, and a translation that confused them would blank the very field the user must correct and would also lose the evidence of which branch ran. CRDNAMEC, CRDSTCDC and EXPMONC take no DFHRED, because :1263-1272, :1274-1283 and :1287-1296 all test flags that 1230, 1240 and 1250 set ISVALID. EXPDAYC carries DFHBMDAR from the unconditional MOVE at :1285. Two further attribute writes land on xxxA items, which are the attribute REDEFINES of the xxxF flag bytes rather than the xxxC colour items this contract admits, so they are recorded here in the audit trail instead: :1309-1313 moves DFHBMBRY to INFOMSGA because WS-INFO-MSG is not blank, and :1315-1317 leaves FKEYSCA alone because PROMPT-FOR-CONFIRMATION is false. Colours are named by their common/BmsAttributes mnemonics throughout rather than by raw bytes, so a failing comparison reports 'DFHRED' and not 0xF2. The :1238-1241 arm is nonetheless taken, since CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET is the 'COCRDLI' the card list left there, and it moves DFHDFCOL to ACCTSIDC and CARDSIDC - which is the x'00' that :1053 had already written, a genuine branch with no observable effect, and saying so is cheaper than wondering later. 3300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS' protection matrix at :1172-1208 matches the arm group at :1181-1190, WHEN CCUP-SHOW-DETAILS / WHEN CCUP-CHANGES-NOT-OK, because 'E' satisfies the second: DFHBMPRF goes to ACCTSIDA and CARDSIDA, the two search keys now protected, and DFHBMFSE to CRDNAMEA, CRDSTCDA, EXPMONA and EXPYEARA, the four fields the user may still edit, with EXPDAYA commented out at :1185. Those five also land on xxxA items and are likewise recorded here rather than in the attributes member. The cursor EVALUATE at :1211-1235 is ordered, moves -1 exactly once, and THIS CASE IS THE ONE THAT TRAVERSES IT IN FULL. FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT at :1212 is an 88 on WS-INFO-MSG, and although :668 did set it, 3250 has since OVERWRITTEN WS-INFO-MSG with PROMPT-FOR-CHANGES - 3250 runs before 3300 per the call order at :1036-1045 - so the first arm group no longer matches; NO-CHANGES-DETECTED at :1213 is an 88 on WS-RETURN-MSG, which now holds the year text, so it fails too; the account arms at :1215-1216 and the card arms at :1218-1219 fail on the ISVALID filters; the name arms at :1221-1222 fail because 1230 set FLG-CARDNAME-ISVALID; the status arms at :1224-1225 fail because 1240 set FLG-CARDSTATUS-ISVALID; the month arms at :1227-1228 fail because 1250 set FLG-CARDEXPMON-ISVALID; and the FIRST MATCH is WHEN FLG-CARDEXPYEAR-NOT-OK at :1230, which moves -1 into EXPYEARL at :1232. That arm is the LAST NON-DEFAULT ARM of the chain, so this case proves the chain is walked all the way down without any earlier arm short-circuiting it and without falling through to the WHEN OTHER at :1233-1234, which would have parked the cursor on ACCTSIDL instead.
